newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan police find decapitated body of schoolboy.
newsitem.headline: Japan police find decapitated body of schoolboy.

text.p: Investigators in the central Japan port city of Kobe on Tuesday searched for a killer after they found the decapitated body and head of a missing 11-year-old boy with a hand-written message that appeared to taunt police.

"Try to catch me!" said a message written with a red pen on a piece of paper stuck in the mouth of Jun Hase, whose head was found in the area of his Kobe home and whose body was discovered later near the school he attended, police said.
Hase, 11, a student at Kobe's Tainohata Elementary School, had been missing since Saturday when he left his house saying he was going to visit his grandfather's house nearby, police said.
The boy was apparently decapitated with a sharp knife and had cuts on his lips and other parts of his head, police said.

The boy's head was found about 500 meters (yards) from another Kobe elementary school, two of whose female students were assaulted by a knife-wielding man in March. One of the victims, a 10-year-old girl, later died from her injuries.
Police are investigating whether the attacks on the children are connected, while students at the dead boy's school were warned not to walk the streets alone or talk to strangers, officials said.
